title: The Swineherd and the Princess

full_text:
The noble young prince offered his kingdom's sacred rose and the miraculous singing nightingale to the emperor's daughter, only to be rejected with haughty disgust because they were real and living.

Disguised as a dirty swineherd, the prince fashioned a magical pot with chiming bells and a musical rattle, demanding kisses from the princess in the mud.

When the emperor discovered the disgraceful barter and banished them both, the prince revealed his royal majesty, rebuking her shallow vanity and shutting the palace gates against her forever.
moral: Scorning genuine gifts of nature and affection for artificial novelties ends in disgrace.
